gallery.title: File:Ballinamore Golf Club bridge - geograph.org.uk - 1308922.jpg
gallery.description:
Ballinamore Golf Club bridge. This bridge links the club house (to the left) with the course of the Ballinamore Golf Club. This is not the only example of a bridge erected by a golf club over a significant waterway - see 484746. 
The bridge spans the Shannon-Erne Waterway. The Waterway is a major canal restoration project, completed in 1994, which links the two principal river systems of Ireland - the Shannon at Leitrim village with the Erne downstream from Belturbet. 

The road in the photograph is followed by the Kingfisher Trail, the first long-distance cycle route to be established in Ireland, which crosses and recrosses the Border in a 270 Km long figure of eight.
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland
Republic of Ireland photographs taken on 2009-05-07

gallery.title: File:Kingfisher Trail and Shannon-Erne Waterway - geograph.org.uk - 1308918.jpg
gallery.description:
Kingfisher Trail and Shannon-Erne Waterway The Kingfisher Trail, the first long-distance cycle route to be established in Ireland, crosses and recrosses the border in a 270 Km long figure of eight.
Over the section between Ballyduff and Ballinamore, the Kingfisher Trail follows the bank of the Shannon-Erne Waterway.The Waterway is a major canal restoration project, completed in 1994, which links the two principal river systems of Ireland - the Shannon at Leitrim village with the Erne downstream from Belturbet.

gallery.title: File:Kingfisher Trail on the outskirts of Ballinamore - geograph.org.uk - 1308943.jpg
gallery.description:
Kingfisher Trail on the outskirts of Ballinamore The Kingfisher Trail, the first long-distance cycle route to be established in Ireland, crosses and recrosses the border in a 270 Km long figure of eight.
Over the section between Ballyduff and Ballinamore, the Kingfisher Trail follows the bank of the Shannon-Erne Waterway.The Waterway is a major canal restoration project, completed in 1994, which links the two principal river systems of Ireland - the Shannon at Leitrim village with the Erne downstream from Belturbet.

Blocks of flats flank the canal on the western outskirts of Ballinamore.

gallery.filename: North shore of Kiltybardan Lough - geograph.org.uk - 1308389.jpg
gallery.title: File:North shore of Kiltybardan Lough - geograph.org.uk - 1308389.jpg
gallery.description:
North shore of Kiltybardan Lough The Irish lakeland of County Cavan and adjoining areas is dotted with innumerable small loughs nestling between the drumlins. Kiltybardan Lough lies within the south-eastern corner of County Leitrim and forms part of the Shannon-Erne Waterway. 
The R208 Carrick-on-Shannon to Ballinamore main road runs along the north shore of the lough, making it much more accessible than most of the loughs in the region.

gallery.title: File:Shannon-Erne Waterway at Leitrim village - geograph.org.uk - 1654541.jpg
gallery.description: Shannon-Erne Waterway at Leitrim village The Shannon-Erne Waterway is a major cross-border initiative linking the two main river basins of Ireland - the Shannon and the Erne via a series of loughs and interconnecting canals. This image is a short way from the Shannon end of the Waterway.
